'''Barry M. Mitchell''' (25 June 1933 – 26 January 2021) was a Canadian<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematician:Barry M. Mitchell - ProofWiki |url=https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Mathematician:Barry_M._Mitchell |access-date=2025-08-24 |website=proofwiki.org}}</ref> mathematician known for his contribution in [[category theory]]. He wrote one of the earliest books on category theory (1965).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Mitchell |first=Barry |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zA2oAAAAIAAJ |title=Theory of Categories |date=1965 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-12-499250-4 |language=en}}</ref>

He proved what is now known as [[Mitchell's embedding theorem]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mitchell |first=Barry |date=1964 |title=The Full Imbedding Theorem |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2373027 |journal=American Journal of Mathematics |volume=86 |issue=3 |pages=619–637 |doi=10.2307/2373027 |jstor=2373027 |issn=0002-9327|url-access=subscription }}</ref> also known as ''Freyd-Mitchell embedding theorem or full  imbedding  theorem.'' This is a well-known result about [[abelian category|abelian categories]].

== Education and academic life ==
He graduated from the University of Toronto with both his bachelor's and master's degrees and obtained his Ph.D. at Brown University. His PhD advisor is [[David Buchsbaum|David Alvin Buchsbaum]] and thesis title is ''Homological Tic Tac Toe''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Barry Mitchell - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=4366 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811150112/https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=4366 |archive-date=2024-08-11 |access-date=2025-08-24 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

He taught at Columbia University, Bowdoin College, and Rutgers University during his academic career.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Barry Mitchell Obituary (1933 - 2021) - Kingston, NY - Daily Freeman |url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/dailyfreeman/name/barry-mitchell-obituary?id=12474478 |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=Legacy.com}}</ref> Among his works are two textbooks: Calculus Without Analytic Geometry and the pioneering Theory of Categories.<ref name=":1" />
